title: Tool components: an ER collet clamps a range of shank diameters

body:
## Problem

The built-in ER collets of #3898 (PR to follow, stacked on #4271) have one exact bore each: whole millimetres from the ER table (`holder_library::ER_SIZES`).

The fit rule `ConnectionCode::takes` compares a plain bore with a shank within 0.02 mm. Thus a collet takes only a shank of its nominal bore.

A real ER collet clamps a range. The range goes from the nominal bore down by 0.5 mm (ER11) or 1 mm (ER16 and larger). For this reason, these shanks of the starter catalogue find no built-in collet:

- the inch shanks 3.175 mm, 6.35 mm and 12.7 mm;
- the drill shanks such as 4.2 mm, 6.8 mm and 10.2 mm.

## Proposal

Give a collet a clamping range on its tool side. Let the fit rule accept a shank in that range.

- Put the clamping range of each series in the ER table, next to `min_bore` and `max_bore`.
- Add a tool-side connection code with a range, or a collet-specific check in `component_fit`.
- Keep the exact match for a plain bore that is not a collet (a shrink-fit or a hydraulic holder).

## Done means

- A 6.35 mm shank fits the `ER32 collet 7 mm`, and a 5.9 mm shank does not.
- "Show compatible parts" on a built-in 1/4 in tool lists its collets.
- The resolver tests stay green. A new test pins the range limits of each series.

The fit rule decides which parts the stack accepts. It is under the safety floor, so the issue is `effort:high`.

body:
Part of #4023. Follow-up of #4254. It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**).

## What happens

The fix of #4254 lets a stay-down link end with an approach from the air: a straight stretch from the air to the start of an open piece on the stock edge. The proof makes sure that the approach cuts no stock off the planned curve.

The approach can arrive at full width. On the dog bone (motion pin `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`, Outside), one approach arrives at full width at (-2.40, 25.00) on the top stock edge. For its last tool radius the disc cuts as a slot (180 degrees). The reading goes from `worst 167, full 0` to `worst 180, full 1`.

The load stage (K3) reads the cuts. It does not read the links. Thus no stage names or slows this full-width stretch.

## What to do

- Let the load stage (or the link stage) read the engagement of the approach stretch of a stay link.
- Name the full-width stretch, or slow the feed on it, as K3 does for a full-width stretch of a cut.
- Alternatively, prove an approach that arrives with less engagement, for example an approach that comes in along a stretch that a cut already made has cleared.

## Done means

The full-width approach on the dog bone is named or slowed by the plan, and the motion pin reads it. No new constant makes stock open.

body:
Part of #4023. A step before the first recipe (K6, #3752). It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**).

## What happens

The kernel gives a `Plan` (entries, cuts, links, lifts, the exit). No production code turns a `Plan` into a `Toolpath`. Only a test helper does it (`kernel_path` in `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k4_order_link.rs`). The design record puts the real converter in `camcraft-motion`, which calls the kernel.

## What to do

Add the converter in `camcraft-motion`:

- Input: a kernel `Plan` for one level, the heights (clearance, retract, feed height, the level Z), the feeds, and the level list (the step-downs).
- Output: a `Toolpath` with the same move types that the old planners emit: rapids, plunges or the moves of the entry, feeds, arcs for exact circles and arc leads, the retract, and the notes. Each lift writes its named reason to the notes in the form that the old links use, so the status line and the law measures read it.
- The converter adds no decision of its own. It emits what the plan holds, in the plan's order. It refuses a plan step that it cannot emit, with a named reason. It never drops a step and never adds a cut.
- A rapid is emitted only at or above the clearance height. A feed below the stock top is emitted only for a step that the plan proved (a cut, a link, an entry, an exit).
- Levels: the same plan shape at each Z level, with the level transition that the entry stage gives (the entry of the next level), and the present level order.
- No old planner changes. With the default switch the output is identical.

## Pins

- Unit tests on hand-made plans: each step kind gives the expected moves; a lift gives a retract with its reason in the notes; an unknown step is refused.
- The motion `kernel_laws` K4 pin uses the real converter in place of the test helper, with the same counts.
- The verifier of `camcraft-sim` finds no rapid into stock and no plunge without an entry on the converted disc and dog-bone plans.

## Done means

The converter is on the side branch with its pins green, and the first recipe (#3752) can call it.

title: Sim playback draws a posed rotary tool about its own tip - the work-turning rotary's kinematics are not shown
body:
﻿## What happens

In the simulation playback of a rotary program (a rotary that turns the work about a horizontal line, e.g. a Rotary Flow on a mill-turn with an A rotary), an indexed/posed station is drawn with the whole tool assembly - shank, holder, spindle housing - rotating about the TOOL TIP, while the work stays at its document pose. The tool visibly swings from radial to pointing down, driving the 250 mm housing far below the table.

The playback timeline carries only a tool tip and a tool-axis vector (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs:188-218`, `:602-632` - a posed move is stored as an A/B/C letter, never a work transform), and the renderer poses the tool about the tip with a shortest-rotation map (`crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs:151-177`), reading no rotary axis line (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs:313-348`).

## Why it matters

The drawn motion is kinematically wrong for a work-turning rotary: the machine turns the WORK about the rotary line while the tool stays upright. The playback shows the opposite, which reads as a collision that does not exist and hides the one that could. Display-only today (the post gate runs its own math), but it trains the user's eye on the wrong kinematics.

## Suggested behaviour

At an indexed pose, draw the work rotated about the stated rotary axis line and the tool upright (or at minimum, draw the tool upright at the tip station and note the simplification), matching the machine-frame kinematics the gate judges with.

Suggested labels: P7, area:ui, effort:medium, source:agent.

title: Post gate: spindle housing strikes the machine table at index poses on a work-turning rotary - frame question
body:
﻿## What happens

A Rotary Flow operation on a part mounted along the machine X axis, machined on a Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A, turns the work), is refused at post with:

```
Flow1: spindle housing at move 3 strikes a fixture
Flow1: spindle housing at move 99 strikes a fixture
```

The reporter states no fixture and no workholding beyond the machine table. The only "fixture" in the judged set is the machine-derived table (`MACHINE_TABLE`, folded into the fixture boxes). Moves 3 and 99 are early approach/link moves, not deep cuts.

## The kinematic question

The rotary table turns the WORK; the table steel is fixed in the machine frame. The spindle housing only reaches the table's Z band if the tool descends beside the part into it - at approach/link stations with a normal stick-out, a housing-table strike is surprising. Two candidate explanations:

1. A frame bug: the housing pose or the table box is judged in the wrong frame at an indexed pose (the table box rotated with the part's frame, or the housing pose not transformed into the machine frame), so the check refuses a legal program.
2. A real catch: the holder is short, the A index deep (-86.250 deg), and the housing genuinely enters the table's swept band at those stations.

The reporter believes (1): "the table rotary turns, but the table doesn't - so the tool can't hit the table unless it goes way down in Z."

## Reproduction

Small cylinder (R 9, 30 long) mounted along X, stock 30 x 44 x 44, Rotary Flow with a 3 mm ball, nose-to-axis stated on the setup, post to the Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table. The refusal names moves 3 and 99. The project file is available from the reporter.

## What the fix should settle

- Which frame the housing band and the fixed table box are judged in at an indexed pose.
- Whether the refused poses are legal (the refusal is phantom) or the finding is real and the message should say WHICH steel was struck (it names no box today - "a fixture" for a user with no fixture reads as a bug).

Suggested labels: P3, area:post, effort:high, source:agent.

body:
Found while working #4026 (K3, the load stage, on branch `issue/4026-kernel-load-control`).

What happens: the motion pin `kernel_laws::k3_load::kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` reads the kernel plan round the disc and the dog bone with the law measures of #4154 (60 degree limit, tool radius 4, step 2). On the Outside start, some feed moves read above the limit, and the load stage does not name a place within one tool radius of them:

| Case | None (no load control) | Constant engagement 25 % |
|---|---|---|
| disc Outside | 13 of 402 over moves | 74 of 334 over moves |
| dog bone Outside | 3 of 724 over moves | 66 of 678 over moves |

The Inside start has 0 (None) and 1 (constant engagement; a link feed, not a cut) unnamed moves.

The unnamed moves are on the stock edge line (`y = -25` or `x = -40`), at the ends of ring pieces that start after a lift. At those places the kernel read (`crates/pathkernel/src/load/law.rs`) gives ae/D 0.0 to 0.13. The meter of #4154 (`crates/motion/tests/common/law_measure/engage.rs`, rim of `mask_grid.rs::contact_width`) reads more than 62.5 degrees.

Expected: the two reads agree within the read tolerance, or the kernel read is the higher one. Then each move above the limit is named (law L6).

Possible causes to check: the raster cells on the stock boundary (`Region::contains` on the edge); the first read of a piece after an entry; the direction of the first feed of a piece.

Done means: the pin shows 0 unnamed moves on the Outside rows, or each one that stays has a named reason, and the cause is in the K3 decision file.

title: i18n part 3: route UI strings through tr()/tf() in batches (split of #853)
body:
## Sub-issue of #853 — Part 3: route UI strings through `tr()`/`tf()`, in batches

**Proposal, asking for a yes before any code lands.** Follow-up to the closure of #3304.

### What

Move user-visible literals to catalogue keys, one batch per PR:

1. `crates/ui` — static literals at direct egui call sites (`on_hover_text`, `label`, `button`, `checkbox`, `menu_item`), shared property vocabulary, ribbon/tree/page captions, help text, status banners. About 100 files (commits `01fb6f18`, `e2ab79fe`, `b818cf79`).
2. `crates/ui` — dynamic `format!` templates through `tf()`, so Chinese can reorder words; arguments are pre-rendered and substituted in the translated template order. About 171 files (commit `19eed997`).
3. `crates/app` — status, refusal and error text; each refusal keeps a stable name or code. About 354 files (commit `89172375`, plus `7f212d12` and `0093244c`).

Each batch opens its own PR. No batch may be combined with another.

### Why batches

The closed #3304 changed 589 files in one PR. Splitting by crate and by static/dynamic seam makes each diff reviewable and keeps a failing batch revertible without disturbing the others.

### Rules

- English is the key. A miss shows English, never a key or a blank.
- Never route G-code, CL, project files, `.mch`/`.cps`, MCP names/JSON, parsed log lines or test goldens through the catalogue.
- Structural scripts must report 0 missing keys before a batch is proposed.
- Tests and AccessKit checks match by stable ids, not English labels.

### Acceptance

- App fully in Chinese for the batch's surface, with English fallback for any untranslated key.
- Posted output byte-identical in every language.
- `scripts/i18n/check.py` exits 0.

### Depends on

Part 1 and Part 2. Each batch is independent of the later batches.

body:
Part of #4023. Follow-up of #4241 (PR #4253) and of K4 (#4177). It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**).

## What happens

For the material side Outside, the kernel plan lifts 13 times on the disc band and 15 times on the dog-bone band. Each lift has a named reason. The design record (K0, #4024) has the target of 0 lifts on the disc, and the old 2D Offset planner has 0 there.

PR #4253 lets a link run in the band outside the stock and along the air. The lifts stay, because the last stretch is not proved: the way from the air back in to the start of the next piece. Each of those starts is more than 0.9 tool radius from each finished cut, so the link would go over uncut stock.

## What to do

The design record decided for #3934 that the split pieces of an Outside band are joined as the Adaptive air plan joins them. Apply that to the last stretch:

- Each ring that is cut open at the stock edge has its two ends on the stock outline. The order stage can start such a piece at an end that the air reaches.
- The approach from the air to that end is an entry in air in the cut plane (law 5): the tool comes from the air and starts to cut along the planned curve. It does not go over uncut stock off a curve. Prove the approach with the proof of the entry stage (the lead-in of an air entry), not with a new assumption.
- A piece whose ends are not at the stock edge keeps the present rule. If no proved way exists, the lift stays and has its named reason.
- Do not make a strip of uncut stock "open" by a constant. The review of PR #4234 found that defect one time.

## Pins

- Negative tests first: an approach from the air that would cut uncut stock off the curve is refused; an approach near a keep-out at the stock edge is refused; an approach beside a part that reaches out of the stock is refused.
- The law suite (`order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named`) and the motion pin (`kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`) are measured again, with no tuning of a constant. Give the counts as measured. For each lift that stays on the disc, say which link has no proof and why.
- Inside and Outside still cut the same curves (law 3). 0 crossing feeds.

## Done means

The Outside lift counts on the disc band and the dog-bone band are measured again with the proved approach, each lift that stays has its named reason, and the pins are green. If the count on the disc is not 0, the PR says exactly what blocks it.

﻿## What happens

When a Rotary Flow (or the rotary twins) resolves its rotation axis, the resolved line has no readback: the machine editor shows the machine's stated rotary axis, the operation editor shows an operator-stated axis, but a fitted axis (the resolver's last step) is invisible in the UI. The fit's only traces are the band note's R figure and the heights' behaviour.

## Why it matters

A user who turns or moves a part cannot see where the fit landed, or whether it landed where they expect, until the cut is generated - and a wrong-axis surprise is a surprise at generation time, not at pick time.

## Suggested behaviour

Show the resolved axis in the operation editor for the rotary kinds: the source (machine / stated / fitted) and the line (a point and a direction, or "through the work offset origin, direction X Y Z"). Read-only is enough.

body:
## Summary

This issue is a proposal from the two UI owners. It shows the target workspace in two mockups. It also gives the plan: the issues and pull requests that we intend to make, and the release order.

We ask the maintainer to read it and to answer the questions at the end. We do not file the sub-issues before the maintainer answers.

## Goal and limits

- CamCraft must feel like a CAM tool. A person who knows a CAM system must find the setup tree, the operation properties, Generate, Simulate and Post without a manual.
- The workspace must work on a small screen. Each side pane folds, so the viewport gets more space.
- No change in this plan changes a toolpath or posted G-code. The UI pull requests change only the look, the layout and the messages.
- Each change from the UI stays an undoable command. The MCP tools stay the same.
- Clean room: the mockups are our own drawings. We used no text, icons, layout or screenshots from another CAM product.

## Mockups

Both mockups are 1366 × 768. The source file is a FigCraft file in our design notes.

### E1: all panes open

![E1: all panes open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E1-proposal.png)

- Title bar: menu bar, Save, Undo and Redo, and document tabs. The second tab shows the target. Until CamCraft can open more than one file, there is one tab. The magnifier is a placeholder for a command search.
- Ribbon: a machine-mode list ("Milling") and workflow tabs in program order: Setup, 2D, 3D, Drill, Multi-axis, Simulate, Post. The ribbon shows only the groups of the selected tab.
- Browser: the setup first (stock, machine, then the operations in program order). Each operation shows its state as a symbol and a word: current, never, calculating (elapsed time), stale, failed. "Machine: not set · Choose…" is a warning that you can click.
- Viewport: the height planes have a key with the name of the operation, and labels in the scene.
- Properties: the operation editor has six groups: Tool and cutting data, Geometry, Heights, Passes, Entry and linking, Accuracy and output. A folded group shows its values on one line. Each height shows its reference, its offset and the result: "= Z 10.000 in G54". A badge shows the source of each value: default, template, derived or set. A disabled button tells why it is disabled. Delete is in the ⋯ menu.
- Issues pane, below the viewport: each issue names its cause and has one button that goes to the fix. A check that did not run shows as "unavailable", never as "passed". The running job shows its elapsed time and Cancel.

### E2: all panes folded

![E2: all panes folded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E2-proposal-folded.png)

- A folded side pane becomes a title chip on the viewport. The viewport then uses the full width. A click on a chip opens the pane again. The camera does not move when a pane folds or opens.
- Each chip keeps the safety state as text. The Browser chip shows the counts of failed and stale operations. The Properties chip shows the state of the operation.
- The issues pane folds to one line. The line keeps the counts and the running job with Cancel.
- The move-type key lists only the move types that the project contains. A hover tag on a move shows the operation, the move type and the feed rate.

Parts of E1 and E2 need engine work first: the source badges, the "failed" state, and a stop inside the generators. The section "Plan, step 2" names them.

## What CamCraft has today

We checked the code on `main`:

- Heights already have a reference and an offset (`HeightReference` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/height.rs`). The UI can show the result now.
- An operation has three states: Never, Ok and Stale (`OpStatus` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).
- The windowed app generates toolpaths on a worker thread, with a progress overlay and Cancel (#2257). Cancel discards the result, but the worker continues to the end.
- The toolpath data has three move kinds: Rapid, Feed and Plunge (`crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs`).
- CamCraft opens one project at a time.

## Plan, step 1: UI work on what exists

These pull requests change no engine data. Each one is a `feat` PR in the enhancement lane, `P6`. Each one keeps toolpaths and posts the same, updates its `layout_page_*` and structural tests, and keeps the `crates/ui` test count (#1953).

| PR | Content | Effort | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| R | Refactor: split `panes.rs` (1665 lines) into ribbon, tabs and status bar files. No visible change. | medium | - |
| A | Theme: palette, a monospace font for numbers, the last colour literals into tokens (#1120, #4209). | medium | - |
| E | One command table and an in-app menu bar. The ribbon reads the same table. | high | R |
| D | Title bar with one document tab, the machine-mode list with workflow tabs, a ribbon that folds, status bar chips. All machine modes in one PR. | high | E |
| P | Side panes fold to title chips. The saved panel setups (#2339) keep the fold state. View ▸ Reset layout. | medium | R |
| C1 | Viewport: the heights key, plane labels in the scene, line patterns for the planes, the Display bar. | medium | A |
| C2 | The move-type key for the three move kinds, filtered to the project, and a hover tag on a move (operation · move type · feed). | medium | C1 |

body:
Found during the review fix of PR #4234 (issue #4177, K4 of the path kernel).

What happens:
- `region_build::region` makes the cutter-centre area of an `Outside` region end at the stock outline.
- The air of the region starts one tool radius outside the stock (`s.offset(2r) - s.offset(r)`).
- A link sample between the stock outline and the air is in neither area. The link proof refuses it (`CUTS_PART`).
- After the fix of PR #4234, the strip just inside the stock edge is uncut stock until a cut clears it (`UNCUT_STOCK`).
- Thus the link from one piece at the stock edge to the next piece cannot stay down. The motion `kernel_laws` k4 pin reads 13 lifts on the disc band and 15 lifts on the dog-bone band (Outside). Each lift has a named reason. The old 2D Offset planner has 0 there.

The old ring links (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs`, `AIR`) let a link leave the stock: a centre outside the stock by 0.1 tool radius counts as air. Its tool then cuts at most 0.9 tool radius into the stock.

What to examine:
- A free band outside the stock where a link may run: outside the stock by 0.1 r or more, and away from the part by the tool radius plus the leave (the part can touch the stock edge).
- The proof that such a band cuts no part wall and no keep-out area.
- The new lift counts on the disc band and the dog-bone band.

Done means: the link proof can run a link through the proved band outside the stock. The lift counts of `order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named` and `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` are measured again, and each remaining lift has its named reason.

title: Heidenhain DIN/ISO post: native peck cycles rapid back to the last depth (G205 Q258=0, G200 Q200=0), and PECK posts full retracts

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post

labels.name: in-review

body:
What happens: the Heidenhain DIN/ISO post writes native peck cycles that do not do the motion of the checked chain. The post writes a native peck only when the R clearance is 0, so Q200 is always 0.
- PECK posts `G205` with `Q258=+0 Q259=+0` and `Q257` equal to `Q202`. The chip-break depth is the plunging depth, so the control makes a full retract after each infeed. Then it moves at FMAX back to 0 mm above the last depth (the advance stop distance is 0). The chain makes only small chip-break hops and feeds down.
- DEEP posts `G200` with `Q202` = the peck and `Q200=+0`. After each infeed, cycle 200 retracts and then moves at FMAX to the set-up clearance above the last depth. With Q200=0, that is the last depth itself. The chain rapids up to R and then feeds down from R.
- In both cases the tool moves at FMAX to the cut face in the hole. The simulation and the gouge check read the chain, so they do not see these moves. The comment at `heidenhain.cps:858-859` says the post wants "a conservative feed re-approach". The words do the opposite.

Expected: the native cycle does the motion of the checked chain, or the post writes the explicit chain.
- After a full retract, the tool goes back at FMAX only to a positive advance distance above the last depth. It feeds the remaining distance.
- PECK posts chip breaks inside the infeed, not a full retract after each peck.
- DEEP does not rapid to 0 mm above the last depth.

Evidence (upstream/main `1c0152c91`):
- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:814`: PECK selects `G205`, DEEP selects `G200`.
- `heidenhain.cps:844-850`: a native peck only when the clearance is 0. Else the post writes the explicit chain.

title: UI: pilot a 2D Contour Properties refit
body:
## Problem

The 2D Contour operation page puts its identity, state, fields and actions into one narrow pane.

The user can find the controls, but the page does not group the operation context, path state and next action with equal clarity.

The pane must also remain usable at 1366 by 768, at a larger UI scale and beside a long refusal.

## Proposal

Refit the shared operation Properties pane through the 2D Contour case.

The pilot keeps the current egui shell, dock, viewport, commands, undo history, project data and generated toolpaths.

The pilot uses original CamCraft tokens and icons. It does not copy SolidCraft UI kit code, theme values, fonts or icons.

The pilot has three presentation parts:

- A header that names the operation, its type, setup, source, tool and work offset.
- A visible path state that shows never generated, current, stale or blocked with the existing details and focus links.
- A fixed action band that keeps Generate primary and Apply, Clear toolpath, Close and Delete distinct.

Keep the existing tabs:

- Geometry.
- Heights.
- Passes.
- Lead in / Lead out.
- Feeds.

Use the existing form seam in `layout/form.rs` and `fields.rs` for rows, groups, fields, units, status and actions.

Do not add a parallel widget set.

## Behavior contract

- A parameter edit keeps the current staging behavior.
- Apply keeps its current undoable command.
- Generate keeps its current apply-and-compute behavior.
- Clear toolpath keeps the operation and removes the path.
- Delete keeps its current command and undo behavior.
- An unavailable control says why in the existing accessible hover or status surface.
- Stale, warning and refusal text comes from the existing operation and post data.
- A global operation does not show an explicit setup that it does not have.
- The renderer, picking, camera, simulation and post logic do not move into the page or widget code.
- A still frame does not rebuild derived geometry or regenerate a path because the page changed.

## Scope

This issue covers a 2D Contour Properties pilot and the small shared components that the pilot needs.

The pilot does not add:

- A new UI engine.
- A SolidCraft dependency.
- A second panel host.
- A ribbon or docking rewrite.
- A command or parameter change.
- A project format change.
- A toolpath, collision, verification or post change.
- Finish passes or spring passes.
- A pixel snapshot update.

The paused SolidCraft adoption work in #655 is separate. The open form-seam umbrella #1122 is separate and owns its listed page-family slices.

The pilot must stop and stack when it reaches a current PR or held code range instead of editing that range on a second branch.

## Verification

Use the Contour fixture from the example catalog.

Check these cases:

- The pane at 1366 by 768.
- The pane at a narrow dock width.
- The pane at a larger UI scale.
- Light and dark built-in themes.
- A field with a unit.
- A long refusal.
- A keyboard-only tab and action walk.
- A screen-reader name for each action and field.
- Apply, Generate, Clear toolpath, Close and Delete routes.
- Undo and redo after an edit.
- Never generated, current, stale and blocked states.
- Existing stale-path and post-refusal wording.
- No geometry cache rebuild from a layout-only change.
- The current operation layout test and staged-number edit test.
- The quick gate for the final diff.

## Documentation and decision record

Record what the pilot keeps, what it changes and what it drops.

The record names the Contour header, state banner and action-band decision.

Do not write the decision into `RECOMMENDED.md`.

## Done means

- The Contour Properties pane follows the proposed hierarchy in the running app.
- The existing tabs, values, commands, status data and generated paths remain unchanged.
- The shared components draw through the existing form seam.
- Light and dark states read at common desktop and narrow widths.
- Apply, Generate, Clear, Close and Delete keep their current behavior.
- Stale paths and posting blockers remain explicit.
- Keyboard, structural and layout checks pass.
- The quick gate passes on the final head.
- No pixel snapshot or generated output file changes.

title: Picks: a chain pick on a .sc model follows by the pair of SolidCraft face names when the model imports again

labels.name: P8

body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212 and #4213.

**What happens now**
- A chain pick (an edge, or a loop of edges) is also a geometry hash. In the baseline (#3915), 10 of 19 chains were lost after the 60 → 80 mm change.
- One lost chain is the end edge of the top face, the kind of edge that a profile cut follows. Generate refused the 2D Contour on it: "Edge of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- The SolidCraft cache names faces only, not edges. But SolidCraft already uses a pair of face names for an edge: the fillet on the edge between `F2:side:b` and `F2:side:c` is the face `F3:blend(F2:side:b|F2:side:c)`. The lost edge above lies between `F2:side:a` and `F2:bottom`, and both names are in the 80 mm file.

**Need**
- When a `.sc` model imports again, a chain pick on it follows by the pair of SolidCraft face names of each edge.
- A chain that is the whole loop of one face can follow that face.
- The rules of #4213 apply: exactly one candidate, only `verified` names, a visible follow, and a pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report and refused at generate as today.
- The path kernel (#4023; K1 is #4025) turns each pick into a `Chain` and takes geometry, not pick ids. A chain that follows is a normal pick id, so the path kernel needs no change for this.

**Done means**
- On the fixtures of #4212 and #4213:
  - a chain pick on an edge between two named faces follows after a design change;
  - a chain whose face pair is gone, or is not unique, does not follow: the re-import report names it, and generate refuses it as today.
- A model with no names behaves as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Picks: a face pick on a .sc model follows its face by the SolidCraft name when the model imports again

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Part of #3915. Uses #4212.

**What happens now**
- A face pick is a hash of the face geometry (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs:884`). When a design change moves the face or changes its size, the id is gone, and generate refuses the pick: "Face of 'part' is no longer in the model: re-pick it".
- Baseline on 0.27.0 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3915#issuecomment-7201006498): the bracket at 60 mm, then 80 mm. The features of 8 of the 11 SolidCraft faces were lost, and generate refused the operations on them. The 80 mm file holds the same 11 names.
- CamCraft does not guess that a missing face and an added face are the same face: "re-picking is Stage C's decision, made visible to the user, never assumed" (`crates/geometry/src/geometry/revision.rs:17-20`). A SolidCraft name is not a guess. It is SolidCraft's own identity for the face. But the follow must be visible (Q2).

**Need**
- When a `.sc` model imports again, a face pick on it follows its face by its SolidCraft name.
- A pick that cannot follow is named in the re-import report, and generate refuses it as today.
- The geometry still decides. A pick follows only when exactly one new face has the same name set and the same kind (plane, or not a plane).
  - A CamCraft face or patch over several SolidCraft faces has a set of names.
  - A new face whose `former` is equal to an old name counts as a face with that name.
  - A name that is not `verified`: no follow.
- A pick whose id is still in the model does not change.
- Scope: the picks that operations hold (the geometry selection, area picks, "Do not touch" picks, and the pick stores of each kind). Setup, WCS, alignment, fixture and electrode picks behave as today. Start and exit picks are coordinates, not feature ids, so they behave as today.
- The follow also works when the project was saved and opened again, or runs headless, before the new revision arrives.
- The re-import and the follows are one undo step.
- A model with no names behaves as today.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q1. A `PROJECT_VERSION` step?** The follow in a reopened project needs data from the earlier import, so the solution can save data in the project file. If it does, does that data need a version step?
  - `solids` (#917) has no step: "an old reader that drops it reads the soup" (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:637-644`).
  - `source` (#2463) came with v72: "An old reader must refuse a v72 file" (`crates/app/src/project/source_dto.rs:1-5`).
  - Recommended: no step. An old reader that drops the data gives today's behaviour, as with `solids`. A step also lands only at a cut, and older builds then refuse each file that the new build saves.
- **Q2. Follow automatically, or offer the follow?**
  - Follow at re-import, and add a needs-review line to each operation that has a followed pick; or
  - offer the follows as one step that the user or the agent accepts.
  - Recommended: follow, with a needs-review line that names the face, for example "face 'F2:side:b' of 'part' followed by its SolidCraft name after the model was imported again". It is one undo step, it is visible, and `mark_operation_reviewed` clears it (`crates/app/src/mcp/order_tools.rs:24`). Today the `needs_review` field of an operation (`crates/app/src/project/entity.rs:442`) holds migration warnings; this is a second use.
- **Q3. Do `Patch` picks follow in this sub-issue?**
  - Recommended: yes, by name set.
  - 2D Pocket takes a patch pick. In the baseline, the bracket's patch over three SolidCraft faces has the same name set in both files.

**Done means**
- Two revisions of one design, with the same names in a different order (fixtures as Q4 in #4212 decides):
  - a face pick on a face that moved or changed size follows by its name;
  - a `Patch` pick follows by its name set (if Q3 is yes);
  - a pick on a removed face does not follow: the re-import report names it, and generate refuses it as today;
  - an unverified name, two candidates, or a change of kind: no follow;
  - a `former` name follows;
  - each operation with a followed pick shows the follow (as Q2 decides);
  - undo puts back the old picks, and redo makes the follow again;
  - import, save, open, then import again: the follow works.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` with no names: the same behaviour as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Import: keep the SolidCraft source face and its name for each facet of a .sc model

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Part of #3915.

**What happens now**
- A `.sc` model comes from one SolidCraft body. The kernel knows the record face of each triangle (`MachiningMesh::tri_face`, `crates/kernel/src/machining_mesh.rs:46`).
- The import drops it. `push_facets` copies only the three corners (`crates/geometry/src/kernel_import.rs:13-26`).
- The `.sc` reader does not read the face names.
- SolidCraft writes one name for each face of the body record, in record order, in `cache/model.json` at `model.names[n].faces`. Each face also has `info`: `[aliases, bounds, verified, synonyms]`, and from SolidCraft 0.50.0 an optional fifth item, `former`. The research comments in #3915 give the sources and the runs.

**Need**
- After a `.sc` import, CamCraft knows for each facet its source face and the SolidCraft name of that face, with its `verified` flag and its `former` name.
- The import never fails because of names. Name data with a wrong count, a wrong shape or a value out of bounds gives no names, and the import continues as today.
- When the facets change by a different route (for example `repair_model`), the names must not stay on the wrong facets.
- STL, OBJ, STEP and a `.sc` file with no names: no names.
- A user sees no change in behaviour from this sub-issue. The other sub-issues of #3915 (picks, MCP) use the names.

**Questions for the maintainer**
- **Q5. Names from cache format 10 only?**
  - Format 10 is the format of SolidCraft's published names writer (`crates/doc/src/model_cache.rs`).
  - CamCraft knows format 8 only from the sample `testdata/models/solidcraft_for_beginners.sc` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcraft/mod.rs:51-53`), and the reader takes no layout from sample bytes (`mod.rs:15`).
  - Recommended: format 10 only. A format-8 model imports as today, with no names.
- **Q4. Which fixtures?** The options:
  - containers that the tests build in code, with names of our own, as `crates/kernel/tests/solidcraft_import/` already does;
  - `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` (cache format 10, with names);
  - a pair that SolidCraft made from its `examples/bracket.json`, at `width` 60 mm and 80 mm.
  - Recommended: the containers that the tests build, first. Also `hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` if your rule on SolidCraft material permits it. The SolidCraft-made pair only with your permission.
  - The same choice applies to the tests of the other sub-issues.

**Done means**
- After a `.sc` import (cache format 10), each facet has its source face, and the SolidCraft name, `verified` flag and `former` name of that face. `info` with four items and with five items both read.
- A test shows that each facet gets the name of the face that it lies on, not only the correct count of names. (Facets that shift by one also give the correct count.)
- Bad name data gives no names, and the import is OK. The hostile-input tests cover the names part with no panic.
- STL, OBJ, STEP, a format-8 `.sc` and a `.sc` with no names: no names, and the behaviour is the same as today.

I prepared this issue with Claude Code (an AI agent) and checked it.

title: Stock STL export checks the f64 mesh, not the file: corners closer than one float32 step collapse as written; repair::weld keeps one of a back-to-back pair

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_export.rs` states the law "a hole is a refusal": the file must not claim a solid it is not. `machined_mesh` enforces it with `iso::unpaired_edges` (#4122) on the f64 triangles. `stl_bytes` then writes each corner as `f32`. Two corners closer than one float32 step are distinct in the checked mesh and one corner in the file. Their facets are written with a repeated corner, and the edges around them are no longer on exactly two facets. The check passed, but the file is not a closed solid.

One float32 step is 7.6 um at 64 mm, 15.3 um at 150 mm and 30.5 um at 300 mm, while the marching extractor places corners anywhere along a lattice edge. On a cut stock in our lane (31.7M facets, coordinates up to about 216 mm, cell 0.254 mm), the f64 mesh had 0 open and 0 unpaired edges. The file as written had 3 edges on three or more facets and 4 facets with a repeated corner, all at one spot, with corners 4 to 9 um apart where the step is 15 um.

A related gap in `repair::weld` (`crates/geometry`) matters for any fix that welds to the written values. `drop_degenerate` keeps the first of a set of duplicate facets. A closed mesh can weld into a back-to-back pair (the same three corners, opposite windings). Each of its edges is then on two facets of the pair, so dropping only one leaves those three edges odd: the weld opens the mesh it was meant to clean.

Measured on main e6849c5ae, synthetic, through the public `stock_export::stl_bytes` and `repair::weld`:

| Input (closed in f64: 0 open, 0 unpaired) | After | open | unpaired | repeated-corner facets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tetrahedron near 150 mm, edge 0-1 split at a corner 3 um from corner 0 (6 facets) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| thin tetrahedron: corners (150,150,150), (160,150,150) and two corners 3 um apart at (155,155,150) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| the same thin tetrahedron | `repair::weld(.., 5e-6)`: kept 1, dropped 3 | 3 (`open_edge_count`) | | |

The closed answer for the thin tetrahedron is no facets at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. The six facets: (p0, p2, a), (a, p2, p1), (p0, a, p3), (a, p1, p3), (p1, p2, p3), (p0, p3, p2), with p0 = (150, 150, 150), p1 = (160, 150, 150), p2 = (150, 160, 150), p3 = (150, 150, 160) and a = (150 + 3e-6, 150, 150).
2. `iso::unpaired_edges` is 0.
3. `stl_bytes`, then read the corners back as f32: `unpaired_edges` is 3, and 2 facets have a repeated corner.

Expected: the exported file passes the same closed check the export applied.

### Proposed fix

1. In the export, judge the mesh as it will be written. Round each corner to its `f32` value. When any facet collapses there, weld bit-exact on the rounded corners and drop the collapsed facets. Run `unpaired_edges` on that result, and write it or refuse by name. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes byte-identical to today.
2. In `repair::weld` / `drop_degenerate`, drop duplicate facets in pairs: k copies of one corner set keep k mod 2. A duplicate pair puts two uses on each of its edges, so dropping both keeps every other edge's count, and a closed mesh stays closed.

We use (1) in our own lane's writer, through `repair::weld` at 0. Pins: the two synthetic cases above (as written: closed after the fix), and a clean mesh writing byte-identical.

### Version and OS

main e6849c5ae (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `area:geometry`, `P3`.

title: Field engine refuses ordinary moves the column engine cuts: no caller segments a chord past the per-move ceiling

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord whose clipped swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells beyond the tool at rest, and the message asks the caller to segment the move. Since #4079 the module law says segmenting always brings such a chord under the ceiling.

No caller in the crate segments. `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`, the field arm of `Stock::simulate`) and `Stock::simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`) pass each move whole, in chunks of `BATCH_MOVES` moves. So through the public `Stock` API, the field engine refuses ordinary moves that the column engine cuts, and the program has no field result at all.

Measured on main dc3679fb5, synthetic blocks, cell 0.254 mm:

| Move | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 12.7 mm flat endmill, straight X pass 5 mm deep in a 30 mm block, 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 mm | cuts | cuts |
| the same, 300 mm | cuts | refused (the ceiling) |
| 127 mm flat tool, plunge 2 / 4 mm into a 200 x 200 x 30 mm block | cuts | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | cuts | refused |
| undercut disc head 127 mm across (height 3, neck 12.7 mm), plunge 2 / 4 mm (`simulate_undercut`) | (cuts nothing, by law) | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | | refused |

The ceiling is reached by the tool's footprint times its travel, so a wide tool reaches it in a few millimetres and an ordinary endmill on a long pass. A caller that segments by a fixed length still hits it: a 5 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc adds about 4.96M cells.

We found it in our own lane, which segments every move into 5 mm pieces before `simulate_undercut`: three programs with a 127.4 mm slitting disc plunging 15 to 28 mm were refused.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 340.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (20, 50, 25) to (320, 50, 25) with a flat tool of radius 6.35.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut. The ceiling's own answer (segmenting) is applied by the simulator, not left to every caller.

### Proposed fix

In the field arm's callers (`simulate_field_with`, `simulate_undercut`, and the lathe and display arms that chunk the same way), split a chord whose work passes the ceiling into the fewest equal pieces that bring each under it, before `subtract_batch`. `subtract_batch` keeps its refusal as the per-update bound. The work of a straight chord grows with its length, so halving converges, and the number of pieces is bounded by the move's length in cells.

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: P5

body:
The v0.27.0 cut gate (cut.yml, stage gate, 2026-11-26 00:17Z) stopped at step [01] "debug build (--no-run)" after 22.2 min. No test ran and none failed (summary: "0 failed, 1 stalled").

What happened: the step compiled until about 00:25Z. Then three `rust-lld` links ran at the same time (the `camcraft-ui` test binaries, cold build, `-j 4`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`). The links wrote no output for 15 min. The stall watchdog (`xtask/src/watchdog.rs`, default 15 min for a debug step, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` not set) then killed the process tree. The tag stage was skipped.

Why it is a bug: a `--no-run` build step is a build, not a test. A cold link of a large test binary can be silent for longer than a test step. The watchdog cannot tell a slow link from a hang, so a cut on a cold runner can fail with no code fault.

Possible fixes (choose one):
1. Give build steps (`--no-run`) the longer limit that `--release` and `--ignored` steps already get (4x).
2. Count child-process CPU time (rustc, rust-lld, cc) as progress, and stall only when the tree is idle.
3. Set `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN` for the gate step in `cut.yml` (a workaround, not a fix).

Workaround for the current cut: re-run the gate with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN=45` in the cut runner's environment.

Related: #3493 (how the watchdog kills a step; this issue is about when).

Done means: a cold release-tier gate on the cut runner passes step [01] without a stall, and a unit test in `xtask` pins the build-step limit.

body:
## Goal

HEIDENHAIN controls accept different program words per control and per NC software version. Today:
- the Klartext post accepts only iTNC 530 NC 340490-03;
- the DIN/ISO post writes words that are valid only on newer software (#4093, #4094).

The posts should read the control facts that the machine file already states and write the matching dialect. A control or version that a post cannot serve is refused by name.

## The machine file (no new field)

`controller.identity` already holds the facts (#3181, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`):

```json
"controller": {
  "post": "Heidenhain Klartext",
  "identity": { "model": "iTNC 530", "nc_software": "340490-03", "installed_options": ["1", "19"] }
}
```

Proposal: keep the file to facts only. Make the values canonical:
- `model`: as HEIDENHAIN writes it (`TNC 320`, `iTNC 530`, `TNC 640`, `TNC7`, ...).
- `nc_software`: 6-digit ID, `-`, 2-digit release, optional ` SP<n>`.
- `installed_options`: HEIDENHAIN option numbers as strings.

A missing `installed_options` means "unknown": the post refuses or warns for functions that need an option.

## Capability flags (derived from model + NC software + options)

One shared resolver gives each post a flag set. The main flags, each with its HEIDENHAIN version source in the research notes:

- `language.iso`: DIN/ISO exists (none on TNC 124/128/310; TNC 320 from 340 55x-04; TNC 620 from 340 56x-02; TNC 426/430 from 280 472; TNC7 from 81762x-17).
- `blockForm`: `contour`, or `paraxial` for TNC 124/128 (one axis per block, no arcs): refuse.
- `decimals`: 3 (TNC 124/310/410) or 4.
- `toolCallByName`, `toolNameMax` (16, or 32 from TNC 640 34059x-02), `toolDefLR` (false on TNC7 from 81762x-19).
- `drill.c200` / `drill.c205`: the cycle parameter level. Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422. Q208/Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05.
- `oldCycles`: cycles 1/2/17 definable, run-only (iTNC from 340 422) or absent.
- `preset.cycle247`: cycle 247 sets a datum value before iTNC 340 422, and activates a preset-table row after it.
- `dwell`: cycle 9 / `G04 F`, or `FUNCTION DWELL` (TNC 640 -07, TNC 620 -04, TNC 320 -04, TNC7; never on iTNC 530).
- `tilt` (none / cycle 19 / PLANE), `planeAxial`, `planeSym`; `tcpm.kt` / `tcpm.iso` (M128 or FUNCTION TCPM; ISO FUNCTION TCPM only from TNC 640 34059x-10 / TNC 620 81760x-07).
- `m140`, `m136m137`, `feedFzFu`, `arcs.spatial`, `arcs.helixLin`, `q.qs`, `q.qlqr`, `q.formulaPriority2020` (TNC 640 34059x-11: always write parentheses).
- Option gating: tilting needs option 8 (iTNC: 1), TCPM option 9 (iTNC: 2), and on TNC 620 cycles 201-205/208/209 need option 19.

The profile table (control and version range to flag values) is in the research notes. It covers TNC 310, 410, 426/430, iTNC 530 (four profiles), TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640 and TNC7.

## What the posts branch on

- **Klartext:** profile check (replaces the fixed 340490-03 check), tool call form, the `M140` retract or `L Z.. M91/M92`, cycle 247, dwell form, and later the drilling cycles and the cycle parameter level.
- **DIN/ISO:** refuse when `language.iso` is false; the G200/G205 parameter level; always `G04 F` for a dwell unless `FUNCTION DWELL` is confirmed for ISO programs; `G247` only with the preset-table meaning; the coordinate format.

## Scope and order

1. The resolver and flags in one place (post engine or a shared post helper), with a table test: control + version → flags.
2. The DIN/ISO post uses it for the fixes in #4093 and #4094 (these can land first with a narrow check, and move to the resolver here).
3. The Klartext post uses it, and serves more than 340490-03.
4. A refusal by name for an unknown model or version (no silent fallback, because cycle 247 changes meaning between versions).

## Done means

- The resolver maps each control/version in the profile table to its flags. A table test pins it.
- Both posts branch on the flags, not on fixed version strings.
- An unknown control or version is refused by name.
- The goldens of the shipped Picomax machine file do not change, except for the fixes of #4093 and #4094.

Source: HEIDENHAIN's public manuals and "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents, collected and compared by the author's agent (notes, not in the repository). Related: #3095, #3181, #4085, #4086, #4087, #4088, #4093, #4094.

body:
### What happened

A cylinder stock wider than about 1000 cells builds on the column backend and is refused on the field backend. The field refusal is not the shared grid gate; it is the per-facet cell budget in `SdfField::from_mesh` (`field_gen.rs`, `MAX_CELLS_PER_FACET` = 1,048,576). `Stock::from_shape` meshes the cylinder with `stock_mesh` (32 segments), so each cap facet is a long thin triangle across the whole radius, and its bounding box spans millions of candidate cells.

Measured on main 3bb6647f6, cell 0.254 mm, height 1 mm:

| Diameter in cells | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 4095 | builds | refused: facet 2 spans 3,306,212 candidate cells; the message asks for the mesh to be tessellated to the cell |
| 2000 | builds | refused: facet 6 spans 1,524,780 candidate cells |
| 1000 | builds | builds |
| 500 | builds | builds |

`backend.rs` says refusals are backend-independent, and names two field-only refusals (watertightness, a chord whose window spans the grid). This is a third, reached by valid stock the column arm accepts.

Found while reworking #4013 (review of the field cylinder gate).

Related (our reading of their titles, not checked against their plans): #589 and #26 retire the column engine; after that, a cylinder stock this wide would build on no backend.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `let shape = StockShape::Cylinder { diameter: 2000.0 * 0.254, height: 1.0 };`
2. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Column, &shape, 0.254)` is `Ok`.
3. `Stock::from_shape(Backend::Field { band: 4 }, &shape, 0.254)` is `Err`, on facet 6's candidate-cell count (1,524,780), not on the grid gate.

Expected: both build, or both refuse by the same gate.

### Proposed fix

Tessellate the field cylinder's mesh to the cell before `from_mesh` (split each cap into triangles whose bounding boxes stay under the budget, as the error message itself asks), or build the cylinder's field from its exact distance instead of a mesh. A pin: a cylinder 2000 cells across builds on both backends.

main 3bb6647f6 (source build), Windows 11.

body:
## The maintainer's words

2026-11-25: "Well we need a unifying approach to this planning and it calls for a motion planning kernel that dictates how motion can be implemented"

## Problem

Strategies have their own pass planners, link code and entry code. The same selection can give rings in one strategy and straight slots in another. A fix in one planner does not reach the others. #3743 designed a shared ring planner for 2D. This issue makes that design one kernel with a contract.

## The pipeline

1. Region: selection (edge, face, chain, points joined by lines), material side, bounds.
2. Guide curves: rings (concentric or morphed), rows, medial lines.
3. Load control: none, trochoidal, constant engagement. It changes a guide curve.
4. Order: start side (inside or outside) and direction.
5. Link: stay at depth. Lift only with a named reason.
6. Entry and exit: air entry, pre-drilled hole, cleared column, helix, ramp, arc, plunge.

A strategy is a set of choices for these stages. A strategy has no planner of its own.

## Laws

- The same region and the same guide choice give the same curves.
- The material side and the start side are separate parameters.
- The start side changes only the order and the start point.
- A fallback is visible. The status line names it.
- An entry into material needs a proof. Else the kernel refuses with a reason.
- A cut above the engagement limit is prevented or named.
- A move that migrates keeps its output. A defect fix is a separate change.

## Names

Use "path kernel" (for example `crates/motion/src/path_kernel/`). "Kernel" already means the geometry kernel and a heavy lane.

## Order of the steps

1. K0, the design record. #3750 can start at the same time, because it keeps its output.
2. K1.
3. K4 (order and link) and K5 (entry and exit).
4. K3 (load control) and K6 (move the strategies).
5. K7 grows with each step.

## Sub-issues

| Step | Content | Issues |
|---|---|---|
| K0 | Design record: stage types, laws, scope | #4024 |
| K1 | Region model: selection, material side, bounds | #4025 |
| K2 | Guide curves | #3750, #3788 |
| K3 | Load control | #4026, #3932, #3933, #3849 |
| K4 | Order and link | #3750, #3757, #3758 |
| K5 | Entry and exit | #3746, #3934, #3759, #3397 |
| K6 | Move the strategies | #3752, #3753, #3754, #3755, #3756, #3760 |
| K7 | One test suite for the laws | #4027 |

## Related issues

- Start and exit picks (#3325, #3327, #3329) stay separate. They use the start point of K4.
- #3323 is `P?`. It is only linked here.
- #3743 and #3741 are the earlier research and report.

## Scope

2D milling comes first. Then the 3D Pocket levels. 3D finishing, multi-axis, turning, sheet and EDM are not in this issue.

## Done means

Each 2D milling strategy plans through the kernel. The K7 suite is green. No strategy has its own ring, link or entry code.

body:
## Problem

The HSM Adaptive plan of one level of the user's bore can cut three times the feed length of the other plan for the same footprint. The fixture is `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` (`the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`). The planner gives one of two plans to each level:

| Plan | Planar feeds | Arcs | Planar feed length | Feed bounding box (tool centre) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 397 | 72 | 334.31 mm | x [-7.497, 7.497], y [-7.497, 7.497] |
| B | 1933 | 918 | 999.92 mm | x [-7.491, 7.481], y [-7.344, 7.486] |

The footprint of each level is the same disc. Plan B cuts about 3 times the length of plan A. Plan B also does not reach the wall in -Y: its feeds stop 0.153 mm short of the reach of plan A. No note tells the user about the longer plan.

Measured on Linux x86_64, release, with a probe in the test (not committed):

- At 940cc5d0e (before the solidcore bump of PR #3802, mesh 6228 facets): Z 10 takes plan B. Z 15 and Z 0 take plan A. Z 5 takes a near variant of A (403 feeds, 79 arcs, 327.81 mm).
- At df899f029 and baad348f1 (after the bump, mesh 5232 facets): Z 15 and Z 5 take plan B. Z 10 and Z 0 take plan A.

The verifier finds no fault in plan B. It is not a gouge. The cost is cycle time, and a wall stock that is not even at that level.

A scout found no cap near 1000 mm or 999 arcs in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/` (`arc_proof.rs:69` prints a sum, not a limit). The spiral loop (`adaptive/core.rs:35`) and the growth loop (`adaptive/grow.rs:163`) can stop with no note.

## Action

- Find why the planner chooses plan B for some outlines of the same disc. The entry corner of the "wall corners rounded" note also changes: (5.30, -5.30) for plan B, (-5.30, -5.30) for plan A.
- Make the level plan stable for the bore, or give a note when a level plan is much longer than needed.
- Then measure the counts of `pocket3d_hsm` again and update its `BORE_PIN` with the reason.

## Notes

- Found during #3886. That issue updated the pin to the current output (4688, 4660, 1980), because the drift comes from the mesh and not from a new plan.
- Effort max: an HSM planner algorithm.

body:
Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750). Step 5 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "Each ring goes around the part in the plane of the cut and stays at depth. The tool does not lift between the parts of one ring."

## What happens

Circular has its own ring code: `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs:233-340` (`rho = rc - stepover * k` at `:289`, the Inside order at `:288`, the rim helix at `:300`). It walks each ring as its own ladder (`run_level_walks` for each ring, `:340`). Each call makes a new `WalkState` with `first: true` (`levels.rs:328-329`). Thus each ring enters again from the clearance height, and each entry goes down into material. The rings are not linked at depth.

## Fix approach

1. Circular gets its rings from `ring_set` with the circle input. The rings stay exact G2/G3 circles at the same radii.
2. One walk for each level over all rings. The link from ring k to ring k+1 is a stepover link at depth by `ring_links` (a radial line or a tangent arc in the cut plane).
3. One entry for each level by `ring_entry`. The rim helix stays as the entry where the tool must enter material.
4. A lift needs a named reason.

## Pins

- `circular_rings_link_at_depth`: a circular pocket with 4 rings has one entry and 0 lifts on each level.
- `circular_rings_unchanged`: the ring radii and the arc count of each ring are the same as on the head before this change.
- Equivalence: the verifier verdicts and the gouge checks of `crates/motion/tests/circular_arcs.rs`, `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` do not change, except the lift and entry counts.

Effort `max`: a new link law for Circular, under the safety floor. Priority P1: a needless lift and an entry into material at each ring.

Done means: Circular rings come from `ring_set`, each level has one entry, and the pins are green.

body:
Implement the core 4-axis cylindrical flow-line toolpath kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow.rs`.

What to build:
- Accept picked 3D guide edge chains, part facets, a rotary `Axis` (provided by the #2772 stated-axis resolver), `RotaryFlowParams`, and `AxisControl`.
- Require a ball-nose tool and at least two guide chains in this first slice; refuse empty, off-model, or single-chain inputs by name.
- Unwrap each chain into continuous cylindrical `(theta, v)` coordinates about `Axis` using `unwrap_near`, and align chain pairs by nearest `2 * pi` offset.
- Parameterize the pair by normalized arc length, compute developed width `(s = R_ref * theta, v)`, and choose pass count from `stepover` or `scallop_stepover(r, tolerance)`.
- Adaptively chord each interpolated flow curve within `ARC_FIT_TOL` / `tolerance`.
- Compute gouge-free radial ball centers `rho_ball(theta, v)` where `min_tri dist(center, tri) >= r` via `closest_pt_tri`, so steep helical flanks never gouge.
- Link passes radially on the retract cylinder (matching `rotary_links`) and emit tool tips via `retip` and `command_axis`.

Provenance: published 4-axis cylindrical unwrapping and iso-parametric flow-line CAM literature; no vendor material consulted.

Depends on #2772 for stated rotary axis resolution on helical models.

Done means: `crates/motion::multiaxis::rotary_flow` generates gouge-free, radially posed passes across multi-turn helical bands on a rotor mesh in `crates/motion/tests/` and refuses invalid or single-chain inputs by name.

Part of #2804

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: User interface and picking

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "make an issue of using cadmpeg as file importer then i suppose.. we could open all common cad parts into camcraft that way."

What is missing: Model > Open reads STEP, STL, OBJ and `.sc`. A part saved in a CAD program's own format must first be exported to STEP by the user.

What cadmpeg is (from its crates.io entry, docs.rs page and `LEGAL.md`, read 2026-11-13; its source and format-support document were not read): a command-line converter and inspector for native CAD files, <https://crates.io/crates/cadmpeg>, Apache-2.0, version 0.6.12, very new (about 575 downloads).
- Reads `.sldprt`, `.f3d`, `.FCStd`, `.ipt`/`.iam`, `.3dm`, `.CATPart`, NX and Creo `.prt`, ACIS `.sat`/`.sab`, IGES, STEP, USD text.
- Writes STEP (AP203/214/242), IGES, USD, its own JSON form, and limited native writers.
- Commands: `convert`, `inspect`, `check`, `diff`, `measure`, `query`, `dump`, `formats`, `dialects`.
- Its docs say it "is not a library"; the per-format codecs are separate optional crates.
- Its legal policy forbids vendor SDKs, decompiled vendor binaries, NDA or leaked material and any circumvention of encryption or DRM; decoders come from files the analyst may hold plus public material, with a provenance declaration per decoder PR. It states it is not legal advice.

Wanted: Model > Open, the viewport drop of issue 1450 and the MCP `import_model` tool accept those formats by converting to STEP and loading the result through the existing STEP importer and the existing undoable import command (no second import path).

Open questions (research first; answers go in comments here, then sub-issues are filed):
1. Route. Recommended: an optional external tool - call `cadmpeg convert` when it is installed, and refuse by name ("install cadmpeg to open .sldprt files") when it is not. No crate is added and none of its code is bundled. The alternative, linking its codec crates, is a new dependency: it needs the maintainer's yes and a `docs/decisions/` entry, and its provenance becomes ours to answer for.
2. Format support. Read cadmpeg's format-support document and try real files (made by us in each program, or files whose terms allow it): which formats convert to a solid our STEP importer loads whole, and which lose faces or come out as surfaces only. Offer only the formats that pass.
3. Clean-room. Confirm on the record that reading a user's part geometry through a third-party tool brings no HSMWorks material into the project (CAM data stored inside a part file is never read), and that cadmpeg's byte-analysis method is not used for our own code.
4. How the tool is found (PATH, a setting), which version is the minimum, and how a missing or too-old tool is reported.
5. Browser build: no external process there; say so in the refusal.

Safety (Prime Directive):
- A conversion that drops geometry must not give a model that looks whole. Run cadmpeg's own `check`, read its exit code and report, and refuse or name what was lost; never machine a silently partial part.
- Units: the converted STEP's units are stated in the import summary; a file with no units asks, never guesses.
- Untrusted input: the external process runs with a time limit and an output-size limit, its temp files go in a fresh directory that is removed afterwards, the file path is passed as an argument (never through a shell string), and a crash, hang or garbage output gives a named error and leaves the project unchanged.
- The converted STEP then passes the STEP importer's own guards (issue 1536 and follow-ups).

Done means (for the research): the five questions answered in comments here, the tried formats listed with their results, and the sub-issues filed (each with one priority, one effort, area, "Done means" and "Part of" this issue); then `needs-research` is dropped and this issue is closed naming them.

There's no thread-mill tool kind.

**Where:** `ToolKind` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:23`) has `Tap` and the lathe `Thread` insert, but no single-form or multi-form thread mill.

**Effect:** thread milling is a common job on small CNC mills (interpolated threads in any material, large or odd sizes, no tap breakage). A vendor tool library can't carry thread mills at all. In one real catalog build, over 300 thread mills had to be left out.

- Simulation and gouge laws for the form.

Effort: max (a new kind, a helical op and the sim).

Requested by the maintainer (2026-11-11), filed by an agent. **Paused (`P?`)**: not open for work until the maintainer sets a priority.

**Goal:** CamCraft can be used in languages other than English, and behaves correctly for users in other locales.

**What it likely covers** (to be confirmed and broken down when the pause is lifted - nothing here is decided):
- **UI text:** every user-visible string (ribbon, tree, pages, dialogs, tooltips, status line, refusals and warnings from generators, verify and the post gate) comes from a translation catalogue instead of a literal in the code, with English as the source and fallback.
- **Language choice:** a setting to pick the language (and "follow the system"), stored with the user's preferences, applied without a restart if practical.
- **Fonts:** bundled fonts that cover the supported scripts (the current set under `assets/ui/fonts/`), under licences that need no attribution.
- **Numbers and units in the UI:** decimal separator and digit grouping per locale when *displaying and typing* values; mm/inch stays a document setting, not a language setting.
- **What must never be localised:** posted G-code, CL files, project files, machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files, MCP tool names and their JSON, log lines agents parse, and test goldens. A decimal comma must never reach a posted number.
- **Refusal and diagnostic text:** translated for the user, but each refusal keeps a stable name or code so tests, MCP clients and issue reports can match it in any language.
- **Tests:** structural/AccessKit tests should match by stable ids rather than English labels, so they hold in every language.
- **Contributing translations:** a file format and a workflow a contributor can use without building the app.

**Open questions for the maintainer:**
1. Which languages first?
2. Translation mechanism (e.g. Fluent, gettext-style catalogues, or a simple key/value file) - it adds a dependency, so it needs a decision.
3. Right-to-left scripts in scope or not?
4. Are the user guide and the documentation site (#688) part of this, or a separate issue?

Done means (once unpaused and broken down): the app runs fully in at least one language besides English, switching language changes every user-visible string, posted output is byte-identical in every language and locale, and a test pins each of those.

No effort label yet: this is an umbrella that will be split into sub-issues, each weighted then.
